title: skills/objectstack-ai: delete_record treats a request naming one matching record as the approval (follow-up of #34340)
body:
repo:objectstack#1 · os-project-manager · session_01FEkQ5nNrLRm8ssuwWcBVcw

Filing gate: follow-up owed by landing work. PR #34453 (closes #34340) carries `Skills-docs: follow-up owed — skills/objectstack-ai/SKILL.md`, and this card is that follow-up.

**Business reason.** An AI agent connected over MCP reads `skills/objectstack-ai/SKILL.md` to learn how `delete_record` behaves. After #34453 lands, the tool's own description says that a request in which the human names the record to delete, with exactly one record matching, is the human's approval: the agent sends `confirm: true` on that call without asking again. When the name matches more than one record, or the request does not identify one record, the agent lists the candidates and asks first. The skill still says "ask the human first, then retry" for every delete, so an agent reading the skill asks a second time for a delete the human already named. The maintainer's ruling quoted on #34340 is that naming one record counts as confirmation. Who benefits: every person deleting a named record through an MCP client.

**What to change (after #34453 merges; the wording must match what landed):**

- `skills/objectstack-ai/SKILL.md`, MCP tools table, the `create_record`, `update_record`, `delete_record` row: replace "ask the human first, then retry" with the rule as the tool description states it after #34453.

**Already handled in #34453:** the MCP-served skill (`packages/mcp/src/skill-md.ts`) and the Console's copy of it, `content/docs/ai/connect-mcp.mdx`, and the gate's refusal message now state the same rule. This card holds only the `skills/**` row.

**Reader who acts.** The skills seat, as a skills-only wording PR (low-risk Tier S arm), after #34453 merges. The PR body reports the whole-file and whole-package before/after line counts that os-dev.md requires for `skills/**`.

Dedupe words (not searched by this thread; the filing seat reads them): `delete_record ask human first`, `named record confirmation`, `skill-md delete_record`, `connect-mcp delete_record permanent`, `34340 skills`.
